expl.summary: Every jet is placed on 16 scales, each a clipped sum of if-statements on jet observables, and each class score adds some scales and subtracts others; the formula agrees with the true label on 80.3% of validation jets. No if-statement uses the jet mass or an observable equal to (m/ΣpT)² (girth2, width, e2_sq): the size of the jet enters through girth (pT-weighted mean ΔR), the spread of the 15 hardest particles (girth2_top15), e2, LHA and τ1. Several scales still follow the mass closely in rank order (neuron 8 with (m/ΣpT)² at 0.707, neuron 12 with the mass at -0.659, neuron 0 with the mass at -0.638), because they are built from thresholds on girth. The g score is dominated by the particle-multiplicity scale (neuron 1, +47%; fixing it at its mean costs 11.6 accuracy points, the most of any neuron), and the q score adds the small-τ1 scale (neuron 9, +22%) and subtracts both the two-subjet scale (neuron 4, -32%) and the multiplicity scale (neuron 1, -22%). Both W and Z scores subtract the wide-jet scale (neuron 8, -25% and -27%) and add the few-particle, moderate-pT scale (neuron 5, +14% and +17%). W and Z are separated by girth windows in place of a mass window: the girth < 0.0817 scale (neuron 0) adds to the W score (+11%) and takes from the Z score (-20%), while the scales for girth between 0.081 and 0.098 (neuron 7) and between 0.070 and 0.087 (neuron 14) take from the W score (-7% and -8%). The t score subtracts the small-e3, moderate-girth scale (neuron 13, -35%) and adds the large-e2 wide-spread scale (neuron 10, +28%). Neuron 2 (high total pT) enters no class score.

It falls with jet mass, e2_sq, width and (m/ΣpT)² (rank correlations -0.638 and -0.596), none of which it uses. W jets sit highest (1.50), then quarks (0.91), gluons (0.39), Z jets (0.36) and tops (0.11); it is zero for 89.7% of tops and 56.3% of gluons but only 2.2% of W jets.

1.measures: Built from total-pT terms: pushed up for sum_pt > 973 GeV (0.153) and log_sum_pt > 6.91 (0.116), pushed down for sum_pt_top50 > 941 GeV (-0.122) and log_sum_pt < 7.13 (-0.112), plus n_particles > 38.9 (0.064); the difference between the total pT and the pT of the 50 hardest particles makes it grow with the number of particles (rank correlations 0.633 with n_particles, 0.618 with n_pt_above_1, -0.599 with the pT share of the 40 hardest particles). Gluons sit far highest (5.87), then tops (2.98), quarks (2.44), Z (1.84) and W (1.81) jets; it is almost never zero (0.1% of gluons, at most 5.0% for any class).
1.role: It raises the g score (+47%, the largest input of any class score) and lowers the q score (-22%), separating gluons from quarks by multiplicity. It does not enter the W, Z or t scores.

2.role: It does not enter any of the five class scores (all weight shares at most 0.019 in size), so it has almost no effect on the classification.
